Type /bagshops as an admin. Stand where the shop should be and press + New shop at my location . Location: rename the shop or move it to where you stand. Stock & pricing: turn each house on or off and set the bookbag and mini price. The storage fields change slots and weight for every bag of that size. Default positions are already tuned. Use /bagfix only if a bag sits wrong on your server's clothing or peds. Type /bagfix (or /bagfix mini ). A preview bag appears on your character. Pick Bookbag or Mini , a style ( Back , Chest , One strap ) and a part ( Bag , Left strap , Right strap ). Use + and − to move and rotate it. Repeat on a female character. Male and female positions save separately. Copy fixes copies every saved position as text. It is also written to data/prop_fixes.json and printed in the server console.

Job Center. Browse jobs by category and see each one's description, pay, vehicle, deposit and duties, then sign up. GPS is set to that job's depot. Depot. Talk to the supervisor and start the shift. The player changes into the job's uniform and the work vehicle spawns with keys and a full tank. A refundable deposit is taken from the bank. Work. Each task is marked on the map. The on-screen time card shows tasks done, the running total and what to do next. Tasks are done by walking to the yellow marker and pressing E . Clock out. Tasks keep coming until the player heads back to the depot and clocks out. A pay stub shows tasks times pay per task, every bonus, the deposit refund and any damage fee. Their own clothes come back. Ending a shift early At the depot: choose "Clock out and get paid". The vehicle has to be parked back at its spawn point to refund the deposit. Anywhere: type /endshift , press F7 , or target the work vehicle and pick "End shift". A confirm box shows the pay and what happens to the deposit. The deposit is refunded (minus damage) if the work vehicle is within 15 m, otherwise it's forfeited. All of this is set in Config.EndShift : turn it off, change the command or key, set the distance, or pay less than 100% away from the depot ( payPercent ) to reward driving back. If a player disconnects mid-shift, that shift's earnings are forfeited and the vehicle is removed. If the resource restarts, everyone on shift is paid what they had earned plus their deposit.

These seven have their own mechanics. Each one's settings are in its file in config/jobs/ . Dog Walker ( dogwalker.lua ): you keep your own clothes. Owners wait at their doors with 1-4 dogs (more unlock as you complete walks). Each leash is tied to your hand and the dog's neck, hangs with a little slack, and every nearby player sees it. Dogs have breeds and personalities, a happiness meter, bathroom breaks you bag up, and they get bored if you stand around. Pet, treat, sit and play fetch from the dog menu ( G ). Off the leash means a bigger tip, but they can bolt. Lose one and the walk pays nothing. The server picks the dogs and walk time and measures how far you actually walked. Fisherman ( fishing.lua ): you keep your own clothes. Face any water and press E to cast (time the power meter). You stay facing the water with the rod in hand until the fish is landed, and Backspace reels your line back in while you wait (rebindable, so it doesn't clash with hands up on X). Wait out the nibbles (striking early spooks the fish), strike on the bite, then fight it: hold E to reel and ease off when tension spikes, without giving slack. 26 species across fresh, salt and deep water, with bites depending on bait, time of day and weather. Rods upgrade with total catches, and each fish has a real weight. Personal records, plus a dinghy rental for deep-sea grounds. Change bait with G , and sell at the Fish Market. Prospector ( prospecting.lua ): inside a prospecting area (shown on the map during the shift) the detector comes out. Beeps speed up and the signal meter climbs as you close in. Dig with E at full signal. Each area has its own loot, every find has a condition and appraised value, detectors upgrade with total finds, and finds are sold to the Appraiser. Paperboy ( newspaper.lua ): you keep your own clothes. Each route is a random area (Mirror Park, Mirror Park North, Rockford Hills, Vespucci) and you get exactly one throwable newspaper per house. Every house shows on the map with a pink marker; equip a paper and throw it in, any order. Miss and run out and the route is over, no second chances. Ride back to the depot for a new route, or clock out to get paid. The server checks each delivery (distance, that a paper was really thrown, and that you're on the job bike, otherwise it pays $1). Papers can't be put in gloveboxes, trunks or dropped. Mover ( moving.lua ): carry everything to the truck and load it; it sits in the cargo area where everyone can see it. Heavy furniture needs the hand truck from the back of the truck. Drops and crashes damage items (fragile ones more), which lowers the pay. Order Picker ( orderpicker.lua ): uses the large CEO warehouse interior. The shelves only look stocked if your server loads them ( bob74_ipl does by default). Shelf, bench and dock coordinates are estimates: walk it once and fix them with /jccoords . Tow Truck Operator ( tow.lua ): calls come in as breakdowns (the owner waits by the car with the hazards on and tips you), illegally parked cars or accidents (a smashed-up wreck). Back the flatbed up, get out and winch the car on, then haul it to the repair shop or the impound lot and unload it. Pay = base for the call type + a distance bonus - any damage done while it's on your truck. Fishing and prospecting pay by selling items. The other five pay into the paycheck like the rest of the jobs. Recycling Worker Players start at the depot manager outside on Elysian Island and are taken into the recycling warehouse. They grab a bag off the trash pile and get told which color bin it goes in (yellow, blue or green); a wrong bin is rejected. Each correct sort pays payPerTask and has a 50% chance of a bonus item ( metal_scraps , plastic , and blueprint_glock from blue bins). They clock out with the floor supervisor inside and are taken back outside. The server picks each bag's color, so the reward table can't be chosen by the player. Items are given through your inventory (see config/integrations.lua ) and the item names must exist in it. Everything is in config/jobs/recycling.lua . Bus and tour passengers The bus and tour bus carry real NPC riders that every player can see. At each stop a few walk up from the curb and board while you wait, and some get off and walk away. The tour starts with a group already on board. Set it per job with passengers = { start, board, alight, max, models } in the job's file, or remove the block to turn it off.

Crews Jobs with crew set in their file can be worked together, sized to the seats in each job's vehicle: up to 4 for garbage, construction, landscaper, janitor, graffiti removal, news crew, package delivery and postman, and 2 for road crew, lumberjack, electrician and window washer. The food truck seats only the driver, so it stays solo. Someone starts a shift as normal. Anyone else signed up for that job sees them in a Join a crew list at the depot and asks to join, and the leader gets a pop-up to accept. The crew shares the leader's stops and work vehicle (members get keys). Each person does their own part at every stop, and the next stop comes once everyone has finished. Everyone earns their own task pay plus the crew bonus ( Config.Crew , +10% by default). Set crew = 2 (or any number) in a job's file to change its crew size. A crew is also capped at the seats in the leader's actual vehicle, so a swapped-in model can't overfill it. Members can clock out any time. If the leader clocks out or disconnects, the crew is paid out and sent home. Job of the day Each day one job (picked automatically, same for everyone, only jobs that pay per task) pays a bonus ( Config.DailyJob , +25% by default). It's highlighted in the job center and on the depot time card, and locked in for the whole shift at clock-in. Admins can change it with /jcdaily <job> . Work streak Clock out with at least minTasks tasks done on consecutive days and the bonus grows: day 2 +2%, day 3 +4%, up to +10% ( Config.Streak ). Missing a day starts it over. With the level system off, the streak shows in the job center where the level would be. Leaderboard A Leaderboard tab in the job center shows this week's top earners (resets Monday) and all-time records: biggest paycheck, most tasks in one shift, heaviest catch and most valuable find ( Config.Leaderboard ). Every bonus is listed on the pay stub. Settings Config.Crew = { enabled = true, maxSize = 4, -- most players in any crew, leader included bonus = 0.10, -- +10% per task while in a crew requestTimeout = 20, -- seconds the leader has to accept } Config.DailyJob = { enabled = true, bonus = 0.25, -- +25% in that job today exclude = {}, -- e.g. { valet = true } } Config.Streak = { enabled = true, perDay = 0.02, max = 0.10, minTasks = 3, -- tasks needed in a shift for the day to count } Config.Leaderboard = { enabled = true, size = 10 }

Everything for that job is in it: on/off, pay, depot, vehicle, blip, work locations, steps and its uniform. config/jobs/README.txt explains every field. The running total shows on the HUD and is paid in one go at clock-out. Level, crew, job of the day and streak bonuses multiply it, and every bonus is listed on the pay stub. Use /jcpay to see the real $/hour of every job and balance them. Tasks never run out Once a shift starts, tasks keep coming until the player clocks out. Random jobs work through every location in a shuffled order, then reshuffle (never the same spot twice in a row). Ordered jobs (bus, tour) loop back to the first stop.

Copy any file in config/jobs/ and rename it. Inside, change Jobs.<name> and Uniforms.<name> to the new name. Restart. New files are picked up automatically. Most new jobs need no code. Steps are built from these types: Step What happens action Play an animation at the stop. Can place a prop there (a grill, a mailbox) pickup Pick something up from the vehicle or the ground (carry animation and prop) dropoff Put it in the vehicle or at the stop. Can leave a prop behind, like cones serve An NPC customer walks up and you hand them something handoff A customer steps out at the door and takes what you're carrying inside valet A guest car pulls up, you take the keys and park it at drop A stop can have a drop point anywhere on the map (the courier's customer is across town). Steps with at = 'drop' route the player there first. Any step can have count = n or { min, max } , and rounds repeats the whole list. Example steps = { { type = 'pickup', from = 'vehicle', carry = 'box', label = 'Grab materials', icon = 'fa-solid fa-box' }, { type = 'dropoff', to = 'stop', anim = 'putdown', duration = 1200, label = 'Drop materials' }, { type = 'action', anim = 'hammer', duration = 10000, label = 'Hammer framing', icon = 'fa-solid fa-hammer' }, },

Every job can put players in a uniform at clock-in. Their own clothes come back at clock-out. Uniforms work with any clothing script, and rcore_clothing also reloads the player's saved outfit afterwards. Set them in game Admins can set every job's uniform without touching a file: type /jcuniforms and pick a job. Use what I'm wearing: dress your character in your clothing menu, then save it as that job's male or female uniform (whichever character you're on). Clothes, hat, glasses, ears, watch and bracelet are all saved. Preview it on me: try the uniform on. Take off the preview gives you your own clothes back. Turn the uniform off / on: off means players keep their own clothes on that job. Reset to the config file and Copy as Lua work the same as for locations. Players get the new uniform from their next clock-in. Uniforms are saved in the database ( hunchoworld_jobcenter_uniforms ) and loaded again on every restart, on top of the config files. Every change is logged to Discord ( admin logs). Set them in the files Clothing IDs shift between game builds and clothing packs, so treat the included ones as a starting point. Dress your character in the clothing menu the way you want the uniform, then run /jcoutfit (admin). It copies a paste-ready line for uniforms.lua . IDs that don't exist on your server are skipped, so a bad ID never makes a ped invisible. Set uniform = false on a job to skip it. Or skip the files and use /jcuniforms in game. Uniforms set in game sit on top of the files, so you can use both.

The coordinates are starting points, not verified in-game. Work stops snap to the ground automatically, but some will need moving. Stand where you want something and run /jccoords (admin). It copies vec4(x, y, z, heading) to your clipboard. Use the full vec4 for peds and vehicle spawns, and drop the heading for stops: vec3(x, y, z) . Turn on Config.Debug = true to see target zones while you tune. Move them in game Admins can move every location without touching a file: type /jclocations . Pick the Job Center or a job, then the spot: depot supervisor, vehicle spawn, shops, warehouse points, tow drop-offs, boat rental, or a list (work stops, taxi pickups and drop-offs, paper-route houses, fishing and prospecting areas, warehouse shelves, recycling bins). Move it to where I am: walk or drive to the new spot, face the way it should face and press E (Backspace cancels). A see-through ped or vehicle shows exactly where it will stand and which way it faces, with the old spot marked in red. Lists can also add a spot where you stand , delete a spot, and show them all on the map with numbered markers and blips. Teleport there jumps to any spot. Changes apply to everyone right away, with no restart. Peds, blips and markers move on the spot. Players on a shift finish the stop they're on, then get the new spots, and a paper route already in progress keeps its houses. Changes are saved in the database ( hunchoworld_jobcenter_locations ), on top of the config files. Updating the script never wipes them, and Reset to the config file puts any spot back. To keep them in the files instead, use Copy every change as Lua : it copies a ready-to-paste block for each file. Paste each at the bottom of the file named above it, then reset those spots. Every move is logged to Discord ( admin logs).

Logs are set in config/server.lua . That file only loads on the server, so players never receive your webhook URL. In Discord: Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook , then copy its URL. Paste it into webhook and set enabled = true . ServerConfig.Logs = { enabled = true, webhook = 'https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...', username = 'Job Center', avatar = '', bigPaycheck = 4000, -- clock-outs at or above this are highlighted bigSale = 4000, -- shop sales at or above this are highlighted mention = '', -- pinged on flags, e.g. '<@&123456789012345678>' events = { clockIn = true, -- shift started clockOut = true, -- pay, tasks, time, deposit, bonuses crew = true, -- joined / left a crew sale = true, -- sold catches or finds flag = true, -- failed server checks admin = true, -- admin actions, job of the day, new records, location and uniform changes }, } Flags are failed server checks: a task handed in away from the job site, a fish landed faster than possible, a paper "delivered" without one being thrown, someone leaving mid-shift. They can ping a staff role with mention . Messages are batched so Discord's rate limit isn't hit.

Paychecks, vehicle deposits and refunds paid through the bank show in the player's banking history. Money always comes from the framework's bank account, so every banking script works for paying players. This page shows what each one records. Banking script What the player sees hunchoworld_banking Pays and charges through its own exports, so every payment is logged with its reason, e.g. "Job center paycheck" Renewed-Banking A statement line from (or to) the employment office with the reason fd_banking Logs bank changes itself; payments show as from (or to) the employment office with the reason okokBanking A transfer from (or to) "Employment Office: Job center paycheck" qs-banking A bank statement for every payment ps-banking Logs every bank change itself, with its own generic description omes_banking A deposit or withdrawal with the reason esx_banking (ESX) A Deposit or Withdraw line with the amount and balance (it has no reason text) Settings Banking = 'auto', -- or a name from the table, 'custom' or 'none' qs-banking: the statement uses the personal account name personal_main . If yours differs, change QS_ACCOUNT at the top of the qs-banking section in bridge/server/banking.lua . What each payment is called The readable text for each payment is in the TEXT table at the top of bridge/server/banking.lua . Change it to rename "Job center paycheck", "Work vehicle deposit" and so on.

Running an inventory, banking, key, fuel or notification script that isn't supported ? Hook it up in one file, with no other changes: Open bridge/custom.lua . It's never encrypted. Fill in the block for that part. Each block has a working example in its comments. In config/integrations.lua , set that part to 'custom' : Inventory = 'custom', Banking = 'custom', Keys = 'custom', Fuel = 'custom', Notify = 'custom' Only the blocks you switch to 'custom' are used. Errors in your functions are caught and printed to the console, so a mistake can't break a shift. Inventory (server) All four functions are needed. Custom.Inventory = { metadata = true, -- can items hold metadata (fish weight, find value)? false = shops pay a flat price give = function(source, item, count, metadata) if not exports.my_inventory:CanCarryItem(source, item, count) then return false end return exports.my_inventory:AddItem(source, item, count, metadata) == true end, -- every stack of the item: { { slot = 3, count = 2, metadata = {...} }, ... } search = function(source, item) local out = {} for _, s in pairs(exports.my_inventory:GetItemsByName(source, item) or {}) do out[#out + 1] = { slot = s.slot, count = s.amount, metadata = s.info } end return out end, remove = function(source, item, count, metadata, slot) return exports.my_inventory:RemoveItem(source, item, count, slot) == true end, label = function(item) local d = exports.my_inventory:Items(item) return d and d.label or item end, } Banking (server) Money always comes from the framework's bank account. Use whichever option fits your banking script. kind is 'deposit' (money in) or 'withdraw' (money out), and text is the readable reason. Custom.Banking = { -- A) write a history line after the framework paid statement = function(source, amount, text, kind) exports.my_banking:AddTransaction(source, amount, text, kind) end, -- B) your banking script logs every framework money change itself: change the reason it sees -- reason = function(text, kind) return text end, -- C) your banking script holds the money: move it there instead of the framework -- pay = function(source, amount, text) return exports.my_banking:AddMoney(source, amount, text) end, -- charge = function(source, amount, text) return exports.my_banking:RemoveMoney(source, amount, text) end, } charge must return false when the player can't afford it. Vehicle keys (server) Custom.Keys = { give = function(source, vehicle, plate, model) exports.my_keys:GiveKeys(source, plate) end, take = function(source, vehicle, plate, model) exports.my_keys:RemoveKeys(source, plate) end, } Fuel (client) GTA's fuel level and the fuel state bag are already set to full before this runs. Custom.Fuel = { set = function(vehicle, level) exports.my_fuel:SetFuel(vehicle, level) end, } Notifications (client) Custom.Notify = { send = function(message, kind, duration) -- kind: 'inform' | 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' exports.my_notify:Notify('Job Center', message, kind, duration) end, } Adding it properly To make auto find your script, add it to the bridge file for that part instead. Each file has a list of adapters, one per script: Part File Add Inventory bridge/server/inventory.lua An entry in ADAPTERS with give , search , remove , label , and its name in INVENTORIES Banking bridge/server/banking.lua An entry in ADAPTERS with statement , reason or pay / charge , and its name in BANKS Keys bridge/server/keys.lua A line in GIVE and TAKE , and its name in system() ( bridge/client/keys.lua for client-only key scripts) Fuel bridge/client/fuel.lua Its name in the list. Only add to SETTERS if it doesn't use exports[name]:SetFuel(vehicle, level) Notifications bridge/client/notify.lua An entry in SENDERS Target bridge/client/target.lua A branch in each function

h: Giving someone access to one command
x: Command Who What it does /endshift Players End your shift from anywhere. A confirm box shows your pay and what happens to the deposit. Default key F7 (rebind in Settings > Key Bindings > FiveM). Rename or turn off in Config.EndShift . /jcshifts Admin Everyone on shift: job, tasks, earnings, time and crew. Teleport to them, or end their shift with or without pay. /jcpay Admin Pay overview: real $/hour per job, hours worked, average time per task and total paid out, with High / Low markers for balancing. /jcpayreset Admin Clear the pay overview numbers and start fresh. /jcdaily [job] Admin Set today's job of the day, e.g. /jcdaily garbage . No job = back to automatic. /jclocations Admin Move any depot, spawn, shop, stop, house, area, shelf or bin in game. Saved in the database and kept after restarts. /jcuniforms Admin Set any job's uniform from what you're wearing, preview it, or turn it off. Saved in the database and kept after restarts. /jcoutfit Admin Copy your current outfit as a paste-ready uniform for the config files. /jccoords Admin Copy your position as vec4(x, y, z, heading) for the config files. Who counts as an admin is set in config/integrations.lua : the aces in AdminAces ( group.admin by default) on any framework, plus the QBCore permissions or ESX groups in AdminGroups . Giving someone access to one command On any framework you can give a group a single command with an ace, for example: add_ace group.mod command.jcshifts allow

Discord logs ( setup ): shifts started and ended (pay, tasks, time, deposit, bonuses), crews, shop sales, admin actions, new records and flags for failed server checks (a task handed in away from the job site, a fish landed faster than possible, a paper "delivered" without one being thrown, someone leaving mid-shift). Big paychecks and sales are highlighted, and flags can ping a staff role. Messages are batched so Discord's rate limit isn't hit. /jcshifts : everyone on shift, with their job, tasks, earnings, time and crew. Teleport to them, or end their shift with or without pay. /jcpay : the pay overview. Real $/hour for every job from finished shifts (task pay, bonuses and shop sales included), hours worked, average time per task and total paid out. It's sortable, and jobs well above or below the median are marked High or Low so you can balance pay. /jcpayreset clears the numbers to start fresh. /jcdaily [job] : change today's job of the day (no job = back to automatic). /jclocations : move any location in game (see Locations ). /jcuniforms : set job uniforms in game (see Uniforms ).

The server picks every route, so clients can't choose their stops. Each completed task is checked for being in order, the player's distance from the stop, and a minimum time per task. Each task pays the job's fixed payPerTask , set on the server. Pay only goes out at clock-out, at the depot, and leaving mid-shift forfeits it. If the resource restarts, players are paid what they had earned plus their deposit. What the server checks Routes: the server picks every stop. Clients can't choose or skip them. Order: each task must be the next one in the route. Distance: the player must be near the stop ( Config.StopValidationDistance ). Time: a minimum time per task ( minStopTime in each job file). Pay: each task pays the job's payPerTask , set on the server. Shop prices and item rewards are rolled on the server too. Job-specific checks: fish can't be landed faster than possible, papers must really be thrown from the job bike, dog walks measure the distance actually walked. Download Download the resource from keymaster.fivem.net under Granted Assets . Don't have it yet? Get it on the Huncho World Store . Add the resource Put the huncho_npcpolice folder in your resources folder. Keep the folder name huncho_npcpolice . Other scripts call its exports by that name. Start it In server.cfg , start it after your framework and the scripts it uses: ensure ox_lib ensure oxmysql ensure qbx_core # or qb-core / es_extended # ... your inventory, dispatch, prison, garage, banking, mdt ... ensure huncho_npcpolice The database tables ( huncho_npcpolice_records , huncho_npcpolice_warrants , huncho_npcpolice_jail ) are created automatically. Add your illegal items Add your server's illegal items (drugs, black_money , ...) to Config.Search.items in config.lua . The list ships empty on purpose. Every arrest takes these items. See Search, evidence & GSR . Mugshots to Discord (optional) Paste a Discord webhook into MugshotWebhook in server/config_server.lua . That file only runs on the server, so players never see it. Restart and check the console About 3 seconds after the resource starts, the console prints what it found: [huncho_npcpolice] server framework: qbx [huncho_npcpolice] server inventory: ox_inventory [huncho_npcpolice] server prison: rcore_prison [huncho_npcpolice] community service: rcore_prison > built-in If a line shows the wrong script, force it in Config.Bridge (for example Config.Bridge.prison = 'builtin' ). Test it In game, run /npcpolicetest (admin). Units are sent to you, even while police are on duty. Every location in config.lua is set for the vanilla GTA map. If your server uses custom maps or MLOs (a new Mission Row, Bolingbroke, Sandy or Paleto station...), spots left on vanilla coords can put players inside walls or under the map. Walk to each spot in game, run /npcpolicecoords (it prints your position and copies it as a vec4 ), and paste it over the matching coords. Spots Where in the config Booking stations: drop-off, fingerprints, mugshot, holding cells, release Config.Booking.stations Built-in jail: spawn, release, yard task spots, belongings pickup Config.BuiltinJail Prison zones (a jailed player outside every zone counts as free) Config.PrisonCheck Built-in community service area and release Config.CommunityService Gunshot ignore zones (ranges, gun stores) Config.Gunshots Robbery zones (banks, stores, jewelry) Config.Detection.robbery.zones Ambient patrol areas Config.AmbientPatrols Booking stations You can add as many stations as you like. station = 'nearest' picks the closest one. A station can set its own officerUnit (for example 'sheriff' for Sandy Shores) and its own release spot where players walk out after bond or a dismissed case.

Back up your edits Copy your config.lua , server/config_server.lua , locales/ and any custom adapters in bridge/ . Replace the resource Download the new version from keymaster and replace the whole huncho_npcpolice folder. Bought it on the Huncho World Store ? It shows up in Keymaster under your Cfx account. One switch at the top of config.lua : Config.Difficulty = 'normal' -- 'easy' | 'normal' | 'hard' | 'custom' easy normal hard Damage per hit when officers shoot you 6-12 10-18 18-30 Officer accuracy / armour x0.5 x0.75 full Seconds to put hands up / holster a gun 15 12 10 PIT chance, roadblocks, spike strips 25%, 1, no spikes 40%, 1 60%, 2 K9 chance, max units on one player 35%, 3 50%, 5 70%, 6 Seconds out of sight to escape 30 40 45 hard is the full-strength police. custom ignores the presets and uses the config exactly as written. Your own values always win Change any single setting where it normally lives, for example Config.PIT.chance = 30 , Config.K9.chance = 40 or Config.Units.swat.accuracy = 60 , and the difficulty leaves it alone. h: 3. Exports from your own scripts (most reliable)
Adding a crime from your own script
x: There are three ways a crime reaches the NPC police. You can use any mix of them. 1. Your dispatch script (automatic) The resource listens to every supported dispatch script at once. An alert meant for police is matched to a Config.Calls entry in this order: The alert's code. ps-dispatch codes like storerobbery match Config.Calls keys directly. A phrase in its title or message, from Config.DispatchKeywords (for example "shots fired" → shooting ). Config.DefaultCall , if you set one. Alerts containing Config.IgnoreKeywords (panic buttons, officer down, EMS) are skipped. Set Config.Debug = true to see every alert and what it matched in the server console. 2. Built-in detection (no dispatch needed) The resource spots these itself ( Config.Gunshots , Config.Detection ), with any drug or robbery script: Crime How it's spotted Gunshots, fights, carjackings, explosions Watched on the shooter's / attacker's game Drug sales The hand-off animation most drug scripts play next to a local, and with ox_inventory a drug item ( items ) leaving the inventory face to face with a local. chance = % of sales called in Car break-ins Smashing or forcing a locked car while a local can see it ( needWitness ) Robberies Robbery animations (registers, safes, drills, hacking, jewelry cases, lockpicking), a gun out inside a robbery zone with a local there, or aiming at a store clerk Crashing into a police car Pulled over for Reckless Driving ( policecrash ) Ambient patrols Speeding over 85 mph ( speedLimitMph ), brandished guns The call follows the place: a vault drill at Pacific becomes a Pacific bank robbery, and the units sent match. Add your scripts' animations to anims , your MLO robbery spots to zones , and drug labs or job spots to ignoreZones . While officers are on duty, these go to them instead: through the built-in dispatch , or pushed into ps-dispatch, cd_dispatch, core_dispatch, rcore_dispatch or origen_police ( Config.Dispatch.forwardToExternal ). 3. Exports from your own scripts (most reliable) Some anticheats (for example ReaperV4) stop one resource from hearing another's events, which stops method 1. Exports aren't affected. See Exports : -- server side: src = the player committing the crime exports.huncho_npcpolice:Alert(src, 'storerobbery', GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(src))) Turning calls on or off Every entry in Config.Calls has enabled = true . Set it to false and the NPC police never answer that call, from any source: vehicletheft = { enabled = false, charge = 'vehicle_theft', units = { 'patrol' } }, Want to turn off Call Hitting or running over an officer with a car officerram Crashing into a cruiser = pulled over policecrash Speeding speeding Vehicle crimes vehicletheft , carjack , carboosting A switched-off call also stops its keywords: a "house robbery" alert with house robberies off is ignored, not answered as a store robbery. /npcpolicetest still works for every call. Adding a crime from your own script Config.Calls.myrobbery = { charge = 'robbery_store', units = { 'patrol', 'patrol' } } Then send exports.huncho_npcpolice:Alert(src, 'myrobbery') from that script. If it checks a minimum police count before a robbery can start, add the virtual officers: local cops = YourCopCountFunction() if GetResourceState('huncho_npcpolice') == 'started' then cops = cops + exports.huncho_npcpolice:VirtualPoliceCount() end VirtualPoliceCount() returns Config.CountAsPolice while no real police are on duty, and 0 once someone clocks in.

If none of the supported dispatch scripts is running, the resource turns on its own dispatch ( Config.Dispatch.enabled = 'auto' ; true forces it on, false turns it off). Every call (built-in detection, exports from your scripts, ambient patrol sightings) is also sent to on-duty real officers: A notification with the 10-code, call type, street and area, and the suspect (gender, on foot or vehicle + plate) A flashing blip with a search-area circle that fades after blip.time seconds Y ( waypointKey , rebindable) sets GPS to the latest call /npccalls lists recent calls to pick from /911 <message> lets players call the police themselves (caller name + location, call911 ) The NPC police still answer calls while no officers are on duty. Change the codes, titles and blip icons per call in Config.Dispatch.calls .

Units The defaults are vanilla GTA: police / police2 / police3 , sheriff cars, and the riot van for SWAT. Officers are the vanilla cop and sheriff peds with a combat pistol and stun gun, carbine rifles for SWAT. Each unit in Config.Units (patrol, sheriff, SWAT) has its own vehicles , livery , extras , outfits , weapons, accuracy and armour . Addon cars, EUP and addon weapons all work. The K9 handler uses the patrol unit's car, uniform and weapons ( Config.K9 ). A car or ped model that fails to load is skipped and the stock one is used. A weapon that isn't streamed falls back to Config.FallbackWeapons with a console warning. Your own uniform Dress up Put an MP character in the uniform in game. Copy it Run /npcpoliceoutfit . A ready-to-paste block is copied. Paste it Paste it as that unit's male = { ... } , and female = { ... } from a female character. For female SWAT, also raise SWAT's femaleChance . The booking officer at the fingerprint scanner wears the uniform of Config.Booking.officerUnit (or the station's own officerUnit ). Sheriff territory Calls in Sandy Shores, Grapeseed and Paleto Bay are answered by the sheriff ( Config.SheriffAreas ): the first response, backup, roadblocks, the transport car, ambient patrols and the K9 handler. SWAT calls don't change. Sheriff cars carry BCSO plates ( platePrefix ). Add more of Blaine County with GTA zone names in zones (Harmony HARMO , Alamo Sea ALAMO , Grand Senora Desert DESRT , Stab City SLAB , ...), or turn it off with enabled = false . Sirens Units drive to a call without sirens and switch them on within Config.Sirens.responseDistance . Sirens are always on in pursuits and on the ride to the station ( Config.Transport ).

Setting Does Config.OnlyWhenNoPolice = true The NPC police only answer while no real police are on duty (default) Config.MaxPoliceOnDuty = 0 Raise it to help a small force: with 2 they keep answering while 0-2 officers are on duty Config.OnlyWhenNoPolice = false Answer no matter how many officers are on Config.PoliceJobs / Config.PoliceJobType Which jobs count as police Handing off When officers clock in mid-call, Config.Handoff sends a takeover alert with the suspect's location, charges and plate through your dispatch, notifies on-duty officers and puts a blip on the suspect. The NPC police keep following for followTime seconds, or until a real officer is within closeDistance , then break off. Officer-requested backup With the Justice System , real officers can call AI units for backup, cuff and search, chases, checkpoints and an air unit, any time.

English and Spanish are included. The text covers notifications, prompts, the radio chatter, the Bond & Counsel screen and the paperwork screen. Copy a locale Copy locales/en.lua to locales/xx.lua . Translate Change Locales['en'] to Locales['xx'] and translate the strings. Keep the %s placeholders. Switch to it Set Config.Locale = 'xx' .

The call A crime reaches the NPC police ( Calls & alerts ). After Config.ResponseDelay , units spawn out of sight and drive in. The suspect gets a notice that police are on the way ( Config.NotifySuspect ). On scene Officers get out, draw and order the suspect to surrender. The suspect has Config.ComplyTime seconds to put their hands up ( E , Config.SurrenderKey ) and holster any gun. Officers say what's going on over their heads ("You're being stopped for Armed Robbery. Hands up!", Config.Speech ). Running or fighting Runners are chased on foot (officers vault low fences, climb ladders and drop off ledges, Config.OfficerMovement ) and tased within Config.TaserRange . Drivers get a pursuit . Shooting or ramming an officer means they shoot back. Cuffed An officer walks right up ( Config.CloseRange ) and cuffs them. Nothing is done from across the street, through a wall or from another floor. Questions and search Consent questions, a GSR test, the body search and a vehicle search ( Search, evidence & GSR ). Charges without evidence are dropped. Transport and booking A code 3 ride to the nearest station (the suspect can press G to skip after a while), then fingerprints, a mugshot and the holding cell ( Booking ). Prison or release Prison through your script or the built-in jail, or out on bond, a lawyer, community service or a fine ( Jail, warrants & release ). Going down Config.JailOnDeath = true : after the revive an officer comes to the player and arrests them. They have to actually walk there; police can't get into locked areas or houses. Config.JailOnDeath = false : going down ends the response. Config.DownedWarrant = true (default): a downed player who isn't arrested gets a warrant instead. Logging out Logging out mid-arrest ( Config.JailOnDisconnect ) means jail on the next login. Players at home Alerts that don't come from the suspect never pick a player in another instance (house routing bucket) or on another level ( Config.SuspectMaxHeight , house shells).

The stop On ticket-only calls the cruiser follows with its lights on at followDistance and parks parkBehind meters behind the car once it stops ( Config.TrafficStops ). It doesn't ram or PIT. Drive off and it becomes a pursuit . The officer walks up and says why: "I pulled you over for Speeding", "License and registration, please". License, registration & insurance Checked with your own scripts, auto-detected ( Config.Citations ): Check Setting Missing = Driver's license driverLicense Driving Without a License Registration registration Unregistered Vehicle Insurance registration No Proof of Insurance Insurance and registration use m-Insurance when it runs. Without an insurance script, a car with no owner (NPC / stolen) counts as unregistered and insurance is skipped. Paper items: put your registration / insurance item names in registration.items and the player must carry them. With metadata.plate an item only counts for that car ( matchPlate ). Impound: each check has an impoundChance % chance the car is impounded once the ticket is paid. Three strikes: missing papers are a ticket the first two times. The 3rd time caught, the officer arrests you instead of writing a ticket, and you get bond or community service in the holding cell. He warns you on the 2nd time. Set it in Config.Citations.repeatOffense ( arrestAfter , charges , resetOnArrest ). Turn everything off with Config.Citations.checkDocuments = false , or one check with its enabled . Unsupported license or insurance script? Connect it in Other scripts . The citation When every charge has a fine, the officer writes a ticket instead of cuffing. It shows on screen with the violations, fines, plate, location and the officer's signature: Sign & Pay: the fine is taken and they're free to go. Can't pay = arrested. Refuse to sign: arrested. Config.Citations.ticket sets the time to decide ( decideTime ) and what happens if they don't pick ( onTimeout = 'pay' or 'refuse' ). enabled = false goes back to paying automatically. A signed and paid ticket never searches anyone. Crashing into police Hitting an NPC police car ( Config.Detection.policecrash ) gets you pulled over for Reckless Driving . Running turns it into a pursuit.

Pursuit tactics Setting Backup units join the chase Config.PursuitBackup Roadblocks, with spike strips Config.Roadblocks PIT maneuver from the rear quarter Config.PIT Boxing in a car that slows down or stops Config.BoxIn K9 on runners Config.K9 Police helicopter on long chases Config.AirUnit Felony stops A suspect wanted for more than a ticket who stops their car with officers on scene gets a high-risk stop ( Config.FelonyStop ): Cruisers stop back ( standOff ), officers take cover behind their doors with guns on the car. Orders, stepTime seconds each: engine off and step out, then walk back with hands up. Reaching the officers hands over to the normal arrest. Staying in the car gets them pulled out by an officer at the door, plus Resisting . Driving off restarts the chase. Losing sight Once officers can't see the suspect, they search around where they were last seen and the way they were heading ( Config.LostSuspect ): on foot for a runner, along the roads for a driver. They don't head straight for the suspect's real position, and PITs, roadblocks and gunfire pause until they're seen again. The helicopter seeing them guides officers in. Escaping Out of sight for Config.EscapeTime seconds = escaped. The timer doesn't run while an officer is right next to them on the same level ( closeRange ). Escaping gives a warrant . Descriptions Officers note what the suspect wears (top, pants, shoes, mask, hat) and drives ( Config.Descriptions ). A suspect who changed clothes, put on or took off a mask, or switched cars is only recognised up close ( recognizeDistance ). The description goes on the warrant: suspect: male, masked, last seen in a Sultan (ABC123) .

Consent After cuffing, the officer asks for consent to ( Config.Consent ): a gunshot residue test (gun crimes only) a search a vehicle search (for Config.VehicleSearch crimes) Saying no is Failure to Comply : it's added to the charges and fines, and the evidence check is skipped, so they stay arrested even if nothing would have been found ( refusalKeepsCharges ). decideTime and onTimeout set the time to answer. What every arrest takes Setting Illegal items, whatever the arrest is for Config.Search.items (ships empty: add your drugs, black_money ...) The crime's evidence items Config.Evidence.items Guns and ammo Licensed players keep theirs only when it isn't a gun crime and the GSR is negative ESX dirty money as an account (no ox_inventory) Config.Search.dirtyMoneyAccount Charges need evidence Charges listed in Config.Evidence.items only stick if at least one of their items is found ( '@firearm' = any gun). Shooting charges need a gun found, and firing a firearm also needs a positive GSR (positive for gsr.window seconds after firing). Unproven charges are dropped. If the main charge is dropped and only minor ones are left (Resisting, Evading...), the suspect is fined and released instead of jailed ( Config.Evidence.releaseIfOnlyMinorLeft , minorCharges ). Nothing left = uncuffed and let go with no record. Illegal items are still seized first. Vehicle searches For drug, robbery, burglary, gun and car-theft charges (configurable), officers search the trunk and glovebox (ox_inventory). Crime items go to the evidence stash, are listed on the paperwork and count as evidence. With searchIfRefused , refusing still gets the car searched. Evidence stash Seized items go into the huncho_npcpolice_evidence stash (ox_inventory), locked to your police jobs. Config.Search.evidenceStash.groups sets a minimum grade, coords limits where it can be opened. Command Does /npcevidence Open the stash /npcreturn [id] Give a player their items back Items are never handed back automatically by default. Set Config.Search.returnItems.enabled = true to return them after bond or a beaten case ( onRelease ), at the built-in jail pickup ( afterBuiltinJail ) or once out of another prison ( afterPrison ). Items in neverReturn ( '@weapons' = every gun) stay in the stash for good.

At the station The cruiser pulls into the nearest station ( Config.Booking.stations , station = 'nearest' ). The suspect is walked through: Fingerprints at the scanner, taken by the booking officer ( Config.Booking.officerUnit ). Mugshot , posted to Discord with the charges when you set MugshotWebhook in server/config_server.lua (needs screenshot-basic). Holding cell with the arrest paperwork on screen: charges, sentence, fines, items seized. K shows and hides it. Fines are taken in the cell. Then the suspect goes to prison, unless they get out first. Bond & Counsel In the holding cell the suspect presses B ( Config.Bail.key ) to open the Bond & Counsel screen. It shows the bond amount (or why there's none), the lawyer fee and the chance to beat the case, with a review bar and a stamp for the result. Choice When What happens Post bond Every charge is in Config.Bail.bondCharges (minor crimes) Paid = released out the front of the station, no prison Call a lawyer Serious charges (no bond) Config.Lawyer.fee , one try per arrest. beatChance % to have the charges dismissed, fines refunded Plead guilty Any sentence Config.Plea.reduction % off (25 by default), straight to prison. No lawyer after that Community service Minor charges, short sentences Service tasks instead of prison. See Community service Fights Arrests where every charge is in Config.Bail.autoBailCharges (fights) never go to prison. When the holding cell time is up, bail is taken automatically and the suspect walks out (released anyway if they can't pay, noted as unpaid). Bond amount base + (sentence x perUnit) + each charge's bond in amounts then x multiplier, kept between min and max, unpaid fines added Set autoBailAmount for a fixed fight bail. Lawyers can also get a shorter sentence when they lose ( reduceChance , reduction ). Ride to the station Sirens on, code 3 ( Config.Transport ). After Config.Transport.skip.after seconds the suspect can press G to skip the ride and be taken out of the car at the station.

h: Your community service script is used
x: Offered in the holding cell ( Bond & Counsel ) as a swap for prison, for minor charges only ( Config.CommunityService ). Who can get it Every charge has to be in charges . One charge that isn't (a drug sale, a robbery...) rules it out, and the screen names the charge that blocked it. The sentence for those charges is maxSentence or less (15 by default). The repeat-offender boost isn't counted, so priors don't rule it out. Not after pleading guilty. Fight arrests get it next to the automatic bail ( fights = true ). The sentence becomes tasksPerUnit tasks per month, between minTasks and maxTasks . Default charges Assault & Battery, Resisting Arrest, Vandalism, Suspicious Activity, Speeding, Reckless Driving Driving Without a License, Unregistered Vehicle, No Proof of Insurance, Failure to Comply, Poaching, Evading Police Your community service script is used With provider = 'auto' , the first script in order that's running and takes the player gets them. If none do, the built-in one runs. Script How Justice System AssignCommunityService . It runs the service with whatever community service its own config uses, and keeps it in its MDT sleezy_coms AssignService randol_service Needs three exports added (below) bc_communityservice GivePlayerCommunityservice esx_communityservice , mh-communityservice Their server events rcore_prison COMS StartCOMS . Skipped when rcore refuses (COMS turned off) The console shows what it found at start: [huncho_npcpolice] community service: justice > rcore_prison > built-in provider Does 'auto' The first script of order that's running (default) 'builtin' Always the built-in one 'sleezy_coms' (any name from the list) Only that script Your own script instead: external = function(src, tasks, booking) ... return true end . Handed to another script: its own task spots are used, so set them up in that script. For example, the Justice System's are in its Staff Console (World → Community service). With none set there, players get no markers. To always use the built-in one (markers, map blip, GPS, /npcpolicecsedit ), set provider = 'builtin' . Justice System: if its Config.API.allowedResources isn't empty, add huncho_npcpolice to it. Otherwise it refuses, and the next script in order is used. Built-in community service The player is taken to the aircraft carrier and sweeps up at its task spots (the ones sleezy_coms uses; sleezy_coms itself isn't needed and the carrier map is loaded for them). Each spot gets a marker, a blip and a GPS waypoint. When they're done they're released at LSIA ( release ). Leaving the area ( radius around center ) puts them back. Logging out, or not finishing within maxMinutes , means prison after all. Somewhere else: set it up in game (below), or change location , center , radius , release and spots in the config. No spots = random spots around the area. Setting it up in game Run /npcpolicecsedit (admin, editCommand ) and stand where each thing should be: Option Does Set start point here Where players arrive Set area here The area around you (radius you pick); leaving it puts them back Set release point here / No release point Where they're let go when done, or stay where they finish Add task spot here A task spot where you stand, with an optional name ("Sweep the walkway") Show spots Markers, names and map blips for every spot for 2 minutes A spot in the list Teleport to it, or remove it Reset to config.lua Remove everything set in game and use the config again It's saved on the server and survives restarts and updates. Ending it early (staff) /npcpoliceremovecs [id] ( removeCommand , group.admin ) ends a player's community service: Where they are Built-in, sleezy_coms, randol_service, esx_ / mh-communityservice Ended by the command Justice System Its release export when it has one, otherwise through the script it sent them to rcore_prison, bc_communityservice No way for another script to end it: the command tells staff to use their own command (rcore: /removecs ) randol_service exports randol_service only has police commands, so another script can't start it. Add these at the bottom of its sv_service.lua : exports('AssignService', function(src, tasks) local Player = GetPlayer(src) if not Player then return false end local cid = GetPlyIdentifier(Player) tasks = math.min(maxTasks, math.floor(tonumber(tasks) or 0)) if tasks < 1 or players[cid] then return false end players[cid] = { tasksleft = tasks } MySQL.insert.await('INSERT INTO randol_cs (cid, tasksleft) VALUE (?, ?)', {cid, tasks}) TriggerClientEvent('randol_cs:client:sendtoService', src, tasks, true) return true end) exports('RemoveService', function(src) local Player = GetPlayer(src) if not Player then return false end local cid = GetPlyIdentifier(Player) if not players[cid] then return false end players[cid] = nil MySQL.query.await('DELETE FROM randol_cs WHERE cid = ?', {cid}) TriggerClientEvent('randol_cs:client:finishService', src) return true end) exports('GetService', function(src) local Player = GetPlayer(src) if not Player then return nil end local e = players[GetPlyIdentifier(Player)] return e and e.tasksleft or nil end)

Prison Sentences go to your prison script, auto-detected ( Supported resources ). If jailing through it fails, the built-in jail takes over. Jailed players are only ignored inside a prison. A player a prison script calls jailed, but who is outside every Config.PrisonCheck zone (Bolingbroke by default; add your prison MLO), is treated as free. Built-in jail Used when there's no prison script. It holds the player inside Bolingbroke for the sentence, keeps their time through relogs, and releases them outside the gate. Config.BuiltinJail.secondsPerUnit sets how long one sentence unit lasts. Prison tasks: marked spots in the yard, press E , tasks.reduceSeconds off per task. Belongings: players go in with nothing; their items are handed back at a pickup outside the gate. Items in belongings.keep (for example 'phone' ) stay with them. belongings.enabled = false turns it off. /npcunjail [id] releases someone early ( Config.Unjail ). Records Every arrest and citation is recorded (your MDT, the Justice System , or the resource's own tables). Repeat offenders get longer sentences: boostPerPrior per prior arrest, up to maxBoost ( Config.Records ). /npcpoliceclearrecord [id] [yes] wipes everything the NPC police wrote about a character. Officer-written records are kept. Warrants Escaping after police arrived gives a warrant ( Config.Warrants , durationHours ), as does going down without being arrested ( Config.DownedWarrant ). Getting away works ( patrolsArrest = false , default): patrols that see a wanted player leave them alone. The warrant's charges are added the next time they're caught for a new crime, so they're jailed for both. patrolsArrest = true : patrols arrest wanted players on sight, if they still match the description . /npcpoliceclearwarrant [id] clears one. Release cooldown After serving time the NPC police leave that character alone for 15 minutes ( Config.ReleaseCooldown.afterJail ), and for 10 minutes after walking out on bond, a lawyer or auto-bail ( afterBail ). Release is detected for any prison script.

Accomplices More than one suspect can be on a call ( Config.Accomplices ): Players within nearbyRadius of the suspect when units arrive, only if they act involved within watchTime (gun out, mask on, running or driving off). Bystanders who stay calm are left alone. Passengers in the suspect's car once it evades. Anyone who shoots or hits an officer during the call. Each accomplice gets their own smaller response ( units ) and is booked separately. If the main suspect crashes or logs out, the rest of the group gets backup instead. Shooting victims A player being shot at or hit by someone else is the victim for a minute ( Config.Victims , window ). Any alert that lands on them, like firing back in self-defense or a "shots fired" alert raised from their own game, goes to whoever shot them. If the shooter is gone, the alert is dropped. Only another real player counts by default ( npcAttackers = false ). Set it to true to count locals (NPC gangs) too. Whoever fires first is not a victim ( startedItWindow ). Officers (NPC or real) shooting at you never count. Victims are never pulled in as the shooter's accomplice.

Config.Radio : on arrival, shots fired, pursuits, foot chases, backup, losing and spotting the suspect, felony stops, custody and escapes, the suspect: hears a radio click, sees a line of radio chatter at the bottom of the screen (the radio_* texts in the locales), hears the officers say one of GTA's own voice lines ( voiceLines , for example the megaphone "pull over"). The radio never warns a suspect that police are coming. It's only heard with an officer within hearRange (30 m by default), the way you'd really hear their radio. The "units responding" line when a call goes out is off ( toSuspect = false ); set toSuspect = true if you want suspects warned. A voice line GTA doesn't know just stays silent. GTA's police scanner reports are all story-mission lines, so they're off by default; add your own per event in scanner .

Every category can take your own adapter in Lua. Open the template bridge/server/_custom_template.lua , or bridge/client/_custom_template.lua for death, screenshot and prison status. Custom framework example Bridge.register('framework', 'custom', { getIdentifier = function(src) return MyCore.GetCharId(src) end, getCharInfo = function(src) local c = MyCore.GetChar(src) return { firstname = c.first, lastname = c.last, dob = c.dob, gender = c.male and 'male' or 'female' } end, isPolice = function(src) return MyCore.GetJob(src) == 'police' and MyCore.OnDuty(src) end, policeCount = function() return MyCore.CountOnDuty('police') end, getMoney = function(src, account) return MyCore.GetMoney(src, account) end, removeMoney = function(src, account, amount, reason) return MyCore.RemoveMoney(src, account, amount) end, getSourceFromIdentifier = function(id) return MyCore.GetSourceByChar(id) end, onPlayerLoaded = function(cb) AddEventHandler('mycore:charLoaded', cb) end, }) Custom dispatch: call the handler from that dispatch's event (example in the server template), or use the Alert export .

x: Works with the Justice System ( justice_core , sage_justicesystem , hunchoworld_justicesystem , or a renamed copy). It's found by its exports , not its name: start it and the NPC police link up on their own: [huncho_npcpolice] Justice System found: hunchoworld_justicesystem (MDT, dispatch, citations, prison) With no Justice System running, nothing changes. Start both; the order doesn't matter. What officers see Records in the Justice MDT. AI arrests become arrest reports (charges mapped to your penal code, booking number, confiscated items as evidence, impounded plate), AI citations become citations, AI warrants become MDT warrants. All with an AI badge and the unit as author. AI units on the dispatch board and live map , with callsigns like AI-12 . AI activity feed on the police dashboard. Community service goes through the Justice System ( Community service ). What officers can do From the duty wheel → AI units , or the MDT: Order What happens Request backup (1-5 units + reason) Cruisers come with the posture of the reason (below), attach to the officer's call, then hold formation, follow on foot or escort the officer's car Cuff & search target The closest backup unit cuffs the person aimed at (in the Justice System's cuffs) and searches them; the officer gets a search report and picks transport, release or hand over. Runners are chased Chase target On foot or in a vehicle, picked automatically Weapons free / Hold fire / Engage target Rules of engagement Draw weapons / Holster / Set perimeter The posture of the units on scene Hold position / Cover me / Follow me Transport to booking The cuffed suspect is driven to booking and handed over there Set up checkpoint here AI officers stop passing drivers and check license, registration, insurance, warrants / BOLO / stolen plates and ankle monitor curfew Air unit A police helicopter (below) Dismiss units Officer-requested units come any time , also while police are on duty. Backup postures Reason En route On scene Weapons Engage Traffic stop lights only parks behind the officer holstered return fire Felony stop / high risk code 3 fan behind the officer, crews behind their doors aimed at the vehicle on command Robbery / armed subject code 3 perimeter aimed at the suspect on command Shots fired / active shooter code 3 fan / moves with the officer rifles weapons free Pursuit / foot pursuit code 3 joins the pursuit holstered / taser return fire Officer down code 3, fastest close cover rifles return fire Crowd control lights fan baton return fire Welfare check / medical / transport / checkpoint calm parks behind holstered return fire Units never start a fight. They never target on-duty police, EMS or corrections, cuffed or surrendered players, or each other. return_fire = only whoever hurt the officer or a unit; on_command = also the armed person the officer ordered them to engage; weapons_free = also anyone armed and shooting or aiming at police. Air unit A police helicopter ( polmav , pilot + spotter, Config.AirUnit ) is created near the requesting officer and flown by their game. It flies to the area, orbits it (searchlight at night) and climbs away when its flight time is up. With the Justice System: officers call it from the job menu or MDT; the Justice System handles cooldowns, pings and call notes. Long AI pursuits and escapes request it automatically. Without it: the same automatic requests for the NPC police's own chases; on-duty police see the helicopter on the map and get the suspect's position ( pingPolice ). While the helicopter sees the suspect, the NPC police don't lose them. No double records, no double fines Config.Justice (bottom of config.lua ): Setting Does records = 'writethrough' Arrests, citations and warrants are only kept in the Justice MDT (default). 1.26.2 ak47_ambulancejob: no more dead players in jail. The script didn't always see when a player was down, so the arrest went ahead and they stayed dead in jail. Now it follows ak47's own down, death and revive events as well as its exports, so the police wait for the revive like they do with other ambulance scripts. Nobody is jailed dead. Anyone still dead or downed when they're jailed is revived first, using the ambulance script's own revive for ak47_ambulancejob, qb-ambulancejob and esx_ambulancejob, and a plain GTA revive for the rest. Turn it off with Config.ReviveOnJail = false . 1.26.1 Officers deleted by another script. qb-smallresources deletes s_m_y_cop_01 , s_f_y_cop_01 , s_m_y_sheriff_01 and s_f_y_sheriff_01 as they spawn (its Config.BlacklistedPeds ). Officers vanished and the response ended as if they'd been killed. Now an officer who disappears without dying doesn't count as killed. The model is remembered as blocked, new officers are sent once using a model that isn't blocked ( Config.BlockedPedFallbacks ), and the console says which setting to change. A warning also shows at startup when qb-smallresources is running with those models in use. Best fix: remove the cop and sheriff models from Config.BlacklistedPeds in qb-smallresources' config.lua (it already turns off GTA's own cops), or use freemode uniforms with /npcpoliceoutfit . The stun gun no longer shows a false "has no ammo" debug message. 1.26.0 Bookbags are searched. When a suspect is searched, every bag they carry from hunchoworld_bookbags (worn or not) is gone through with the same rules as their pockets. Illegal items, the crime's items and unlicensed guns go to the evidence stash and the seized record used by /npcreturn , and the booking lists them as "(in bag name )". What's in the bags also counts as evidence for the charges. The bag itself stays with them. Needs hunchoworld_bookbags 1.0.4 or newer on ox_inventory, qs-inventory or qb-inventory v2. Turn it off with Config.Search.bags = false . 1.25.3 hunchoworld_essentials licenses. A new license bridge, picked first when the essentials license manager is on. Traffic stops check the essentials driver's license, and at booking players with a valid essentials weapon license keep their guns. Suspended, revoked or expired licenses don't count, and neither do card items (a stolen or fake card is not a license). It uses the same license names as before ( weapon , driver ). 1.25.2 The NPC police leave players real officers already hold. That covers being cuffed or escorted by an officer's script, or riding in the back of a car an on-duty officer drives. No new response starts, and a response in progress stops at once: officers hold fire and leave, with no warrant or charges from the NPC police. An officer has to be close by, so a player can't fake it. 1.25.1 The booking mugshot uploads at 100 KB/s (was 250). FiveM can drop a player who sends latent data too fast ("latent event packet overflow"), so this keeps the upload under that limit. 1.25.0 Set up community service in game. /npcpolicecsedit (admin) sets the start point, the area, the release point and the task spots wherever you stand, with a preview of every spot on the map. It's saved on the server and used instead of the config, and "Reset to config.lua" goes back. No more standing in the holding cell when community service is handed to another script (Justice System, sleezy_coms...). You're walked out of the station if that script didn't move you. Fixed a vector helper that could stop the built-in community service and the officer's walk to the driver's window. 1.24.1 Fixed a script error when being booked in 1.24.0 ( attempt to call a nil value (field 'hasDocCharge') ). Update if you're on 1.24.0. 1.24.0 Three strikes for papers. No license, registration or insurance gets a ticket the first two times. The 3rd time you're caught, you're arrested instead and offered bond or community service in the holding cell ( Config.Citations.repeatOffense ). The officer warns you on the 2nd time, and the count starts over after that arrest. Community service for fights. Assault & Battery arrests now offer community service next to the bail ( Config.CommunityService.fights ). Community service looks at the charges, not your record. Available for Beer Pong, Card Hub, Dominoes, Oh Bih Please, Oh Bih Roulette and Slumlords. Cee-lo and Tumbling Towers are set up by players on the spot, so they don't have permanent tables. Pick the game and the table model. Press Place in front of me . The panel closes and a preview of the table appears. Turn it with the arrow keys or mouse wheel , then press E to put it down ( Backspace cancels). From the list you can Go to or Remove any permanent table. Removing one ends any game on it and refunds the stakes. Permanent tables Where the settings are saved Everything you change in the panel is saved in the server's resource storage (KVP), not in the resource folder. Controls Input Does Mouse Aim Scroll Arc, from a flat line drive to a high lob Hold left mouse Power meter. Release in the green zone Right mouse Cancel the throw R Call a re-rack at the start of your turn Hold X or /beerpongleave Leave the game E (watching) Switch between broadcast, orbit and ball cam How it plays Rules: bounce shots take two cups, balls back, heating up and on fire, re-racks, rebuttal, overtime, last cup slides to the middle, throw clock. Each can be switched off. Drinking: when a cup goes in, the defender drinks it. Every drink makes their meter faster and their aim sway. Bots line up, throw, drink and react, and play by the same physics as players. Money bets are off in bot games unless you allow them. Betting: the host sets a bet per player and the winners split the pot. Watchers can place side bets before the game starts. Unfinished games are refunded if the resource stops. Watching: pick Watch the game from the target menu or lobby. The winner takes the pot (Spades: the winning team splits it; ties split it). Leave before the deal: full refund. Walk off or disconnect mid-game: your buy-in stays in the pot. Item ceelo_dice (Dice) Command /ceelo Games Cee-lo Bank, Head-Up, Pot Run, Street Craps, Over/Under 7, Pig Files games/ceelo/ Controls Key / command Does /ceelo or the Dice item Open "set the table": pick a game, a bet, or free play with bots E near a ring Join G Host / shooter starts the round E on your turn Pick up the dice, shake, throw X Leave between rounds (full refund). In Pig: bank your turn /ceelorules Rules for every game Players can rebind keys in Settings → Key Bindings → FiveM . The games Cee-lo Bank: one banker covers the table. 4-5-6 or trips takes the table, 1-2-3 pays everyone, a point means every fader rolls to beat it. Head-Up: one on one, best of three. Pot Run: everyone antes and gets two lives. Lowest roll loses a life. Last one standing takes the pot. Street Craps: 7 or 11 wins on the come-out, 2, 3 or 12 loses, anything else is the point. Over/Under 7: one player is the house; everyone picks a side. Exactly 7 pays 4 to 1. Pig: one die, bank your turn before a 1 wipes it. First to 100 takes the pot. Money and safety Bets are held in escrow from the moment a player commits until the round settles. The server rolls the dice. Clients only animate what it decided. Leaving between rounds refunds everything. Leaving mid-round (walking more than 10 m away or logging out) forfeits. Offline players still get paid on their next login, including after a restart. What players bet with: Config.Money.account (cash, bank, ESX black money, or any item). Free play and bots Turn on Free play when setting the table. The host can add up to 5 bots, who kneel, scoop the dice, throw and react. Bots only sit at free tables. Bet limits: Config.Money.minBet / maxBet , or the admin panel. Dice: drawn in the world, so no streaming is needed. Size and colours in Config.Dice.drawn . A custom 3D model is optional ( install/custom_dice_model/ ).

Item tumbling_towers (Tumbling Towers Set) Command /tumblingtowers Players Up to 6, NPCs for empty seats Files games/towers/ How it plays Host uses the set (or types /tumblingtowers ). A see-through table and chairs follow where you look: scroll or the arrow keys rotate, E places, Backspace cancels. Menu tabs: Table (seats, NPCs), Stakes (free or cash, shots before you're out), Rules . Other players target a chair and pick Sit down (or walk up and press E ), then Accept and play . The host presses Start . Cash stakes are taken from everyone and your view moves to your chair. Your turn: click a block to slide it out, then click a glowing slot on top to set it down. Knock the tower over and you take a whiskey shot in your chair. The tower is rebuilt and the next player goes first. The host sets how many shots everyone can take: Sudden death (0) , 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 or 10. Fewest shots wins (ties split the pot). Results: the host can Run it back or close the table. Controls Input Does A / D , arrow keys, or right-mouse drag Turn the tower W / S or mouse wheel Lean in / out Q / E Lower / raise your view Mouse Look around while you wait X Back to your chair G (walking past) Watch the game Backspace twice Stand up (forfeits your stake mid-game) If the host leaves, the table closes and stakes are refunded.
